lines.en: You look upset, Mohamed. Did something happen at your driving test this morning? You were so confident yesterday.
lines.pt: Você parece chateada, Mohamed. Aconteceu alguma coisa no seu teste de direção hoje de manhã? Você estava tão confiante ontem.

lines.en: I failed it again. Even though I practiced every weekend, the examiner said I was too nervous at the roundabout.
lines.pt: Reprovei de novo. Mesmo tendo praticado todo fim de semana, a examinadora disse que eu estava nervosa demais na rotatória.

lines.en: Oh no. It's not as if you didn't try. No matter how hard you practice, nerves can ruin a test.
lines.pt: Ai, não. Não é como se você não tivesse tentado. Por mais que você pratique, o nervosismo pode estragar um teste.

lines.en: I panicked as soon as she sat down. My hands were shaking, and I stalled twice before we even left the parking lot.
lines.pt: Entrei em pânico assim que ela sentou. Minhas mãos tremiam, e o carro morreu duas vezes antes de sairmos do estacionamento.

lines.en: That happens to everyone. My cousin failed three times, and now he's a taxi driver. Honestly, the system feels unfair sometimes.
lines.pt: Acontece com todo mundo. Meu primo reprovou três vezes, e agora é taxista. Sinceramente, o sistema parece injusto às vezes.

lines.en: It's not as if I wasn't ready. I took twenty lessons, although the instructor kept changing my schedule.
lines.pt: Não é como se eu não estivesse pronta. Fiz vinte aulas, embora o instrutor vivesse mudando meu horário.

lines.en: That's ridiculous. Did you tell the school? You paid a fortune, and they should at least keep the same teacher for you.
lines.pt: Isso é um absurdo. Você falou com a autoescola? Pagou uma fortuna, e eles deviam ao menos manter o mesmo professor para você.

lines.en: I complained yesterday, but they just offered a discount on the next package. I'm tempted to switch to another school.
lines.pt: Reclamei ontem, mas eles só ofereceram desconto no próximo pacote. Estou tentada a mudar para outra autoescola.

lines.en: Do it. Meanwhile, I'll take you out on Sundays in my dad's car, on quiet roads, so you can practice without pressure.
lines.pt: Faça isso. Enquanto isso, levo você para treinar aos domingos no carro do meu pai, em ruas tranquilas, para você praticar sem pressão.

lines.en: Really? That would help so much. We could drive up toward Dinosaur Ridge, since the road is quiet and the view is worth it.
lines.pt: Sério? Isso ajudaria muito. Podíamos subir em direção a Dinosaur Ridge, já que a estrada é calma e a vista vale a pena.

lines.en: Perfect, it's a plan. Next time you walk in there, take a deep breath, and remember you can only do your best.
lines.pt: Perfeito, combinado. Da próxima vez que você entrar lá, respire fundo e lembre que só pode fazer o seu melhor.

facts.big: it’s not as if / even though / no matter how
facts.label: Concessão
facts.sub: It’s not as if I didn’t try. Even though I practised, I failed. No matter how hard I try, I panic. Sem but na mesma frase.

facts.label: Não é como se
facts.sub: Use it’s not as if + oração para negar uma ideia ou suposição: It’s not as if I didn’t try. Mostra que a pessoa tentou. Pode usar no passado ou no presente.

facts.label: Mesmo que
facts.sub: Even though + oração admite um fato, mas mostra contraste: Even though I practised, I failed. Mais forte que although. Sem but na mesma frase.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: It’s not as if I didn’t try means I really tried.
Even though is followed by a clause.
We say “No matter how hard I try, I still panic”.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: It’s not as if I didn’t try means I really tried. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Even though is followed by a clause. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “No matter how hard I try, I still panic”. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Third time lucky · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a snowy evening in Denver. Marco comes home with a long face. His friend Gina is waiting in the living room. He has just failed his driving test again. Gina listens and tries to cheer him up. Together they look for a solution.

“You look upset, Marco. Did something happen with your driving test?” says Gina. “I failed it again. Even though I practised every weekend, the examiner said I was too nervous.” says Marco. “Oh no. It’s not as if you didn’t try. No matter how hard you practise, nerves can ruin a test.” says Gina.

pages.title: Third time lucky · 2/3
paragraphs: “It’s not as if I was not ready. I took lessons for two months, although the instructor changed my schedule.” says Marco. “Even though it feels unfair, you are improving. It’s not as if you were making the same mistakes as last time.” says Gina. “True, but no matter how patient I try to be, I still panic at roundabouts. It’s not as if there are many here!” says Marco.

“Then ask for one more lesson. Though they are rare, you will need them.” says Gina. “I’d love to, but it’s not as if I have unlimited money. Even though the lessons are useful, they cost a fortune.” says Marco. “I could lend you some. It’s not as if I need it, and no matter what happens, I believe in you.” says Gina.

pages.title: Third time lucky · 3/3
paragraphs: “That’s kind of you, although I’d rather pay you back soon. It’s not as if I want to depend on anybody.” says Marco. “Deal. Even though it’s hard now, you’ll laugh about it when you finally pass, no matter how long it takes.” says Gina. Gina makes tea and finds a map. They plan some practice routes for the weekend.
